faq.q: What is the best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella?
faq.a: The best time is from April to October, with peak sightings between June and September. During these months, water temperatures are warmer (20–24°C), sea conditions are calmer, and dolphin pods are more active near the coast. Winter months from November to March have cooler water and rougher seas, reducing sighting probabilities.

faq.q: What species of dolphins can I see in Marbella?
faq.a: The most common species are the common dolphin and the striped dolphin. Bottlenose dolphins are also occasionally spotted. Pods typically range from 10 to 50 individuals, and you may see them leaping, bow-riding, or feeding. The waters off the Costa del Sol are part of a rich marine ecosystem.

faq.q: How long does it take to reach dolphin spots from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Most dolphin-watching charters from Puerto Banús reach prime areas within 20 to 30 minutes. Captains use local knowledge and often spot dolphins near Cabopino, Cala del Faro, or the waters off the Golden Mile. A typical 2-hour charter gives ample time for sightings.

faq.q: Are morning or afternoon trips better for dolphin watching?
faq.a: Morning departures between 9 and 11 AM generally offer the calmest seas and highest sighting probabilities. However, summer evening trips (5–7 PM) can also be productive, with the added bonus of a sunset. Wind and swell increase by midday, so early starts are recommended.

faq.q: What is the water temperature in Marbella for dolphin watching?
faq.a: Water temperature varies by season: 15–17°C in winter (Dec–Feb), 17–20°C in spring (Mar–May), 20–24°C in summer (Jun–Sep), and 18–21°C in autumn (Oct–Nov). Warmer months are more comfortable for swimming stops, though dolphin activity is high year-round in suitable conditions.

faq.q: Can I see dolphins from a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, many boat rentals in Marbella include dolphin watching as part of the itinerary. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús and includes vessels like the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39, which are ideal for small groups. All charters come with a licensed skipper who knows the best spots.

faq.q: What should I bring for a dolphin-watching trip?
faq.a: Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, a light jacket (even in summer, sea breezes can be cool), and a camera. Our charters include soft drinks, water, beer, wine, and light snacks. If you plan to swim, pack a towel and swimwear.

faq.q: Is dolphin watching guaranteed in Marbella?
faq.a: While no operator can guarantee sightings, the waters off Marbella have a high density of dolphins, especially from April to October. data.body_html:
Marbella’s coastline offers some of the best dolphin watching in the Mediterranean, with sightings possible year-round but peaking between April and October. This guide breaks down the best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella, covering water temperatures, sea conditions, and tips for choosing the right charter from Puerto Banús. Whether you’re planning a family outing or a romantic sunset cruise, knowing the season helps you pick the perfect date.

When Is the Best Time of Year for Dolphin Watching in Marbella?

The optimal window runs from April through October, with June, July, and August offering the highest sighting probabilities. During these months, water temperatures rise to 20–24°C, sea conditions are typically calm, and dolphin pods are more active near the shore. Winter months (November to March) see cooler water (15–17°C) and occasional storms, reducing visibility and dolphin activity. However, even in winter, calm days can yield sightings.

Monthly Breakdown of Dolphin-Watching Conditions

  • January–March: Water 15–17°C. Rough seas possible. Sighting probability: moderate on calm days.
  • April–May: Water 17–20°C. Increasing sunshine and calmer seas. Good for early-season trips.
  • June–August: Water 20–24°C. Peak season. High sighting rates, warm swimming, and long daylight hours.
  • September–October: Water 20–18°C. Still excellent, with fewer crowds. Golden-hour trips are popular.
  • November–December: Water 18–15°C. Lower probability but possible on stable days.

Why Puerto Banús Is the Best Departure Point

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella’s premier marina. The harbour sits just minutes from dolphin-rich waters near Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and the coastline east of the Golden Mile. A 20–30 minute cruise puts you in prime spotting territory. Charters like the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are ideal for small groups, while larger vessels such as the Mangusta 80 offer space for up to 12 guests.

What Dolphins Can You See in Marbella?

The most common species are the common dolphin and the striped dolphin. Bottlenose dolphins appear less frequently. Pods typically range from 10 to 50 individuals, and you may witness them bow-riding, leaping, or feeding. The Costa del Sol’s rich plankton and fish stocks attract these marine mammals year-round.

Best Time of Day for Dolphin Sightings

Morning departures between 9 and 11 AM offer the calmest seas and highest sighting probabilities. Afternoon winds often pick up, creating chop that makes spotting harder. Evening trips (5–7 PM) in summer can also be productive, with the added bonus of a sunset over the Mediterranean. Our sunset cruises combine dolphin watching with golden-hour views.

How to Maximise Your Dolphin-Watching Experience

  • Book a morning charter for the best sea conditions.
  • Choose a boat with a flybridge or open deck for better visibility — the Azimut 58 Flybridge is a top choice.
  • Bring binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens.
  • Listen to the skipper: they use local knowledge and often spot dolphins from a distance.
  • Consider a longer charter (4+ hours) to explore multiple areas.
